subject: Urgent: EvergreenTech runtime regressions after modelpack v3.1-int8
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@evergreentech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in p95 + 502s after your modelpack push

Jonas / Laura,

We rolled into production this morning around 02:30 PT when your team pushed modelpack v3.1-int8. Within the first 30 minutes we started seeing a steady p95 jump from ~180ms to ~540ms on our chat completion hot-path and an increase in 502/5xx responses for requests with long contexts (>1024 tokens). We've attached a short sample of error logs and a screenshot of the Grafana panel showing the spike.

Impact: customer-facing experience is degraded on our billing and search endpoints; roughly 8% of requests are failing with 5xx, and throughput appears to be throttled by backpressure. Our SLA alerts fired and our ops team is getting paged.

We need an immediate rollback or a hotfix. Please confirm:
- Can you roll EvergreenTech back to the prior runtime (v3.0) for our account only?
- If rollback isn't possible within 30–60m, what mitigations can we apply (route to a different model variant, enable decoding fallback, throttle large-context requests)?

I appreciate urgent help — we have an executive call scheduled in 45 minutes and I need something to tell our CEO.

Attached: error-sample.log, grafana-dashboard-screenshot.png

Thanks,
Sam Patel
VP Engineering, EvergreenTech
ops@evergreentech.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@evergreentech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p95 + 502s after your modelpack push

Sam — thanks for the data and the heads-up. I'm escalating to engineering and CS immediately. Short answers up-front: yes, we can do an account-scoped rollback to v3.0 and we can also route a percentage of traffic off the v3.1-int8 variant to a fallback for long-context requests.

I'm looping in Rishi (serving runtime) and Laura (CS lead) so we can stand up a bridge and execute a rollback plan. Can you confirm whether the 5xxs are concentrated on two endpoints (billing/search) or across all routes? Also: are the failing requests predominantly >1k tokens?

Proposed immediate actions (30m):
- We start a 15-minute bridge (invite inbound) and perform an account-scoped rollback to v3.0 on EvergreenTech's shard.
- If rollback is blocked, we'll apply routing rule to send sequences >800 tokens to v3.0 or to a non-quantized variant.
- Engineering will collect a qprofile dump + KV-cache stats and share findings.

I'll update within 10 minutes. Standby.

—Jonas
Head of Customer Success & Escalations, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0192

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Spike in p95 + 502s after your modelpack push

Quick diagnostic from the hotpath nodes we've instrumented:
- Observed decode stalls correlated with KV cache eviction churn. On nodes running the v3.1-int8 kernel, attention micro-kernel appears to reset state when sequence padding crosses the 1024->1k+ boundary; that leads to repeated cache reloads.
- Proxy CPU shows increased context-switching and request queuing; per-node throughput drops by ~30% under identical QPS.
- 502s appear to be application-level timeouts triggered after repeated re-tries from the decoder queue.

Hypothesis: the int8 kernel selection introduced a control-flow path that's sensitive to long sequences, which reduces amortized token throughput and increases tail latency.

Immediate mitigations we can implement (engineering):
1) Account-scoped rollback to v3.0 kernel (fastest route).
2) If rollback takes >20m, we can push a routing rule to send requests with context_length>800 to v3.0 (temp rule).
3) Toggle 'quant-fallback' for the EvergreenTech tenant so that any request that crosses the stall condition is switched to float16 execution. This adds CPU cost but avoids user-facing 5xx.

Attached: qprofile-diagnostic.json (small extract). We'll continue capturing KV-hit/miss histograms. I can be on the bridge in 5.

-rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@evergreentech.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p95 + 502s after your modelpack push

Sam — I am very sorry for the disruption. We are treating EvergreenTech as a P1 and will prioritize the rollback.

What we'll do now:
- 9:40 PT bridge (30m) — invite attached (bridge-invite.ics).
- Jonas will coordinate the account-scoped rollback to v3.0; Rishi will lead the engineering changes.
- If rollback is blocked for any reason we will apply the routing rule to send long-context requests to the non-quantized variant immediately.
- After we stabilize we'll run a short smoke test with your QA and then prepare a postmortem with root cause, timeline, and a remediation plan.

As a gesture of goodwill we will credit EvergreenTech one week of compute and assign a dedicated escalation engineer through the next two weeks.

Please accept my apology and we'll be on the bridge at 9:40.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Redwood Leadership <leadership@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 17:15:00 -08:00
Subject: EvergreenTech escalation — summary and exec ask

Leaders —

Summary (final from today's bridge):
- Cause: v3.1-int8 kernel introduced a long-sequence control path that triggers KV-cache eviction churn on hotpath nodes, causing decode stalls and increased tail latency.
- Impact: EvergreenTech experienced ~30% throughput drop on hotpath and ~8% 5xx rate for >1k token requests for ~45 minutes before rollback.
- Action taken: Account-scoped rollback to v3.0 completed at 11:05 PT; routing rule remained for 2 hours as a safety net. Smoke tests passed and customer traffic returned to baseline.

Immediate follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- Engineering (Rishi): implement kernel fix and regression unit tests for long-sequence handling — ETA 2 business days.
- Product/Release (Marissa): add an automated canary that includes long-context traffic to the v3.x rollout gating — ETA 1 week.
- Customer Success (Laura): deliver postmortem and credit note; coordinate 1:1 remediation call — ETA 48 hours.

Exec ask: approve an exception to the rollout freeze to allow a fast-track patch (small kernel change + CI gate) that Rishi certifies solves the regression. This patch will be release-candiate gated with a targeted canary on non-critical tenants first. Without the exception we risk extended time in hotfix branch that will degrade our ability to ship other dependent fixes.

Related artifacts attached: rollback_plan.md, qprofile-diagnostic.json, bridge-invite.ics
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/EVG-3129, https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/evergreentech/serving-hotpath?panelId=7

—Jonas
Head of Customer Success & Escalations, Redwood Inference
